chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from his father, from al-Barqi, from Muhammad ibn al-Qasim ibn Fudayl, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who bought some of the plots of land of a woman from the family of So-and-so, and wrote for her a document stating that she had received the money, although she had not actually received it. Should he give her the money or withhold it? He said, 'Tell him to withhold it from her with the strongest withholding, for she sold him what she did not own.'

key_terms.بَاعَتْهُ مَا لَمْ تَمْلِكْهُ: She sold him what she did not own
key_terms.قَطَائِع: Plots of land or land parcels

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a seller writes a receipt for payment before actually receiving the money?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Hassan al-Awwan (AS) clarifies the ruling of *bay' al-ma'mun* (sale of what is not yet possessed) by ruling that the buyer should withhold payment, as the seller effectively sold what she did not yet own. This highlights the Shia juristic principle that possession (*qabd*) is a condition for the validity of the sale, ensuring the seller has actual control over the goods before transferring ownership. The ruling underscores the importance of preventing uncertainty (*gharar*) in commercial transactions by linking the transfer of funds to the actual receipt of the commodity.
